message.content: On a wind-scoured Tuesday, Elias found the bottle tucked behind the base of the lantern housing. It wasn’t the verdant green he expected, but a deep, opaque blue that seemed to drink the dim light of his quarters. The stopper was cork, swollen and dark. He wiped the frost from the glass and twisted it free with a grunt of exertion. A note wrapped tight within slipped out. The paper was crisp, devoid of the usual damp rot of the sea. In elegant, fading ink, it read: *"If you are reading this, the storm has passed. Please tell them I made it home."* Elias stared at the words, the lighthouse’s rhythmic sweep painting the counter in slow arcs of white and shadow. He checked the date on the note: fifty years ago. A tear, cold and sudden, traced a path down his cheek. He folded the paper carefully, placing it back in the bottle, and sealed it with a kiss before returning it to its hiding spot. Some messages, he decided, were not meant for the world. He were just meant for someone who understood the loneliness of the light.

messages.content: Write a story of about 150 words about a lighthouse keeper who finds a bottle.
